elements.text: If BP < 90/60, give sodium chloride 0.9% 500mL IV rapidly, repeat until systolic BP > 90. Continue 1L 6 hourly. Stop if breathing worsens.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently for gynaecological/surgical assessment:
elements.text: Give ceftriaxone2 1g IV (avoid diluting with lidocaine 1%) and metronidazole3 400mg orally.

elements.section: Manage and refer urgently for gynaecological/surgical assessment:
elements.text: For pain, give ibuprofen4 400mg 8 hourly with/after food.
ABNORMAL VAGINAL DISCHARGE

1If SBP < 80, pulse ≥ 100, respiratory rate > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness, shock likely. 2If severe penicillin allergy (history of angioedema, anaphylactic shock or bronchospasm), omit ceftriaxone and discuss with doctor. Do not mix Ringer's lactate and IV ceftriaxone. 3Advise no alcohol until 24 hours after last dose of metronidazole. 4Avoid if peptic ulcer, asthma, hypertension, heart failure, kidney disease, pregnant. 5If severe penicillin allergy (history of angioedema, anaphylactic shock or bronchospasm), omit ceftriaxone and increase azithromycin dose to 2g. 6For ceftriaxone 250mg IM injection: dissolve 250mg in 0.9mL lidocaine 1% without adrenaline (epinephrine).
